q: 1. An imaginary line joining the points of equal elevation on the surface of the earth represents
explain: By definition, a contour line is the imaginary line on the ground joining points of equal elevation.

q: 2. The direction of steepest slope on the contour, is
options: at an angle of 45 deg to the contour
at right angles to the contour
explain: The steepest slope at any point on the ground is always along the line perpendicular (at right angles) to the contour at that point, since contours represent equal elevation.

q: 3. Two contour lines, having the same elevation
explain: Two contours of the same elevation can unite/merge together, for example in the case of a vertical cliff, where multiple contour lines coincide at a single line on the map.

q: 4. The angle of intersection of a contour and a ridge line, is
explain: A ridge line runs along the line of steepest ascent, and since contours are always perpendicular to the direction of steepest slope, a contour crosses a ridge (or valley) line at right angles (90 deg).

q: 5. The boundary of water of a still lake, represents ...............
explain: The shoreline of a still body of water is a natural example of a contour line, as all points on the water surface are at the same elevation.

q: 6. The representation of general topography of a very flat terrain is possible only ...............
options: by drawing contours at large interval
by drawing contours at small interval
by giving spot levels at large interval
by giving spot levels to features at close interval
explain: In very flat areas, contour lines are far apart and provide little detail, so spot levels (specific elevations at certain points) are used instead.

q: 7. Contour interval, within the limits of a map ...............
options: may vary according to the configuration
explain: To avoid confusion and allow for accurate reading of slopes, the contour interval must remain the same throughout a single map.

q: 8. The suitable contour interval for a map with scale 1:10000 is ...............
explain: A common rule for contour interval is 25 / (number of cm per km). For 1:10000 (10 cm = 1 km), it would be 2.5m, so 2m is the closest standard interval.

q: 9. A contour map of the area is essential before proceeding with the construction of
explain: For a large-scale earthwork project like a dam, a detailed contour map of the area is essential to plan the reservoir capacity, spillway location, and earthwork volumes.

q: 10. Contour lines
explain: Since a contour represents a closed line of constant elevation, every contour must eventually close upon itself, either within the map sheet or outside its boundary; it cannot simply end abruptly.

q: 11. Which of the following methods of contouring is most suitable for hilly terrain?
explain: Tacheometry is ideal for hilly terrain because it allows for distance and elevation measurements without having to physically chain across rough ground.

q: 12. The contours merge or cross one another on the map in case of
explain: Contours merge (coincide) at a vertical cliff surface, and actually cross one another only in the special case of overhanging ground/caves, so all these listed conditions represent exceptions to the normal rule.

q: 13. Closed contours with higher value inside represents a
explain: When the innermost closed contour has the highest elevation value, it represents a hill (elevated feature).

q: 14. The vertical distance between the elevations represented by adjacent contour lines on a map is called
explain: As defined before, the constant vertical distance between two adjacent contours on a map is the contour interval.

q: 15. The spacing of cross-sections in a hilly country is usually
explain: In hilly terrain, where the ground changes rapidly, cross-sections for contouring/earthwork are usually spaced closer together than in flat country, but as per this text the given standard spacing is taken as 20 m.

q: 16. The angle of intersection of a counter and a ridge line, is .............
explain: Contour lines cross ridge lines and valley lines at right angles (90°).

q: 17. An imaginary line lying throughout on the surface of the earth and preserving a constant inclination to the horizontal, is called .............
explain: A contour gradient is a line that maintains a uniform slope or inclination with the horizontal.

q: 18. From any point on the surface with a given inclination .............
options: only one contour gradient is possible
explain: From a single point, you can go in two directions along the hillside to maintain a specific gradient.

q: 19. Contour lines look to cross each other in case of .............
explain: In the case of an overhanging cliff, a higher contour line can physically overlap or 'cross' a lower contour line on a 2D map projection.

q: 20. Bergchund is a topographical feature in .............
explain: A Bergschrund is a crevasse that forms where a moving glacier ice mass separates from the stagnant ice or rock above.

q: 21. The relief representation on the map can be depicted .............
explain: Relief (topography) can be shown using contours, spot heights, hachures, hill shading, or tinting/layering.

q: 22. For preparation of contour plan for a route survey
options: method of trace contour is used
method of cross profile is used
indirect method of contouring is used
explain: In route surveys for roads or railways, cross-sections (profiles) are taken at regular intervals along the centerline to determine the topography of the narrow strip.

q: 23. Accuracy of elevation of various points obtained from contour map is limited to
explain: The standard acceptable error in interpolated elevations from a contour map is generally taken as half of the contour interval.

q: 24. The tacheometric method of contouring is particularly suitable .............
options: when a contoured map of hill is required
when the area is not very extensive
in surfaces of roads or railways
explain: Tacheometry is ideal for hilly terrain where chaining is difficult or impossible due to steep slopes and obstacles.

q: 25. The space of cross-sections in a hilly country is usually .............
explain: In rugged or hilly terrain, cross-sections are typically spaced every 20m to capture significant changes in topography without excessive labor.

q: 26. The vertical distance between any two consecutive contours is called .............
explain: Contour Interval is the constant vertical distance between successive contour lines.

q: 27. The horizontal distance between any two consecutive contours is called .............
explain: Horizontal Equivalent is the distance between two contour lines measured on a map, which varies according to the steepness of the slope.
